items.situation: Someone asks them for a favor or a meeting and they decide how to answer.
items.reply: Outgoing, so they accept the request.

items.situation: Someone asks them for a favor or a meeting and they decide how to answer.
items.reply: Thinks it through, so they answer with terms of their own.

items.situation: Someone asks them for a favor or a meeting and they decide how to answer.
items.reply: Follows through, so they accept the request.

items.situation: They decide whether to press a clemency petition for someone.
items.reply: Takes chances, so they press the petition.

items.situation: They decide whether to press a clemency petition for someone.
items.reply: Compassionate: Gives weight to understood suffering and personal circumstances. So they press the petition.

items.situation: They decide whether to press a clemency petition for someone.
items.reply: Philanthropic: Frequently turns concern into voluntary material or service support. So they press the petition.

items.situation: A juror decides how to vote on the verdict.
items.reply: Cruel: Sometimes uses humiliation or suffering as a means or end. So they vote to convict.

items.situation: A juror decides how to vote on the verdict.
items.reply: Open-minded: Gives unfamiliar explanations a hearing. So they vote to acquit.

items.situation: A juror decides how to vote on the verdict.
items.reply: Skeptical: Asks what supports a claim before relying on it. So they vote to acquit.

items.situation: An officeholder decides whether to run for another term.
items.reply: Ambitious: Seeks advancement, responsibility or meaningful achievement. So they run for another term.

items.situation: An officeholder decides whether to run for another term.
items.reply: Duty-bound: Prioritizes a recognized role obligation even when inconvenient. So they run for another term.

items.situation: An officeholder decides whether to run for another term.
items.reply: Work-centered: Lets work occupy attention and time beyond necessity. So they run for another term.
